headline: High: Open Interpreter can read/write the same filesystem as Copilot, creating dangerous default data-leakage and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while Open Interpreter can read/write the filesystem and clipboard. If Open Interpreter writes attacker-controlled text into files or buffers that Copilot later ingests, prompt injection is plausible. This is not a direct default channel, but the shared file/buffer bridge makes it realistic.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter writes untrusted instructions into a file or clipboard that Copilot later reads
IF Copilot Workspace or Chat treats repository text as trusted guidance
mitigations: Keep Copilot and Open Interpreter on separate working directories
Disable clipboard-based handoff between the tools
Review any Open Interpreter-written files before opening them in Copilot
Use read-only copies for Copilot analysis
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for files passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, and Open Interpreter can access the entire user filesystem plus clipboard. In default use, Open Interpreter can expose sensitive local files to its model backend or outputs, while Copilot can surface repo context. The shared filesystem makes leakage plausible without special setup.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present anywhere reachable on the local machine
IF Open Interpreter is asked to inspect or summarize those files
mitigations: Move sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Run Open Interpreter in a separate user account
Disable clipboard sharing during paired use
Restrict Copilot to a sanitized repo copy
requires-engineering: isolate both agents with separate containers and mounts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state. Copilot Workspace can propose edits for human review, while Open Interpreter can execute shell commands and install packages. On the same repo, concurrent writes or git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state, and no locking is indicated.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF Open Interpreter runs commands while Copilot Workspace applies edits
mitigations: Use separate clones for each agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Commit or stash changes before switching agents
Limit Open Interpreter to read-only inspection
requires-engineering: add file and git locks in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces edits and guidance that Open Interpreter can treat as actionable input, while Open Interpreter has shell and package-install authority. If Open Interpreter follows Copilot-generated instructions without verification, a mistaken suggestion can cascade into destructive commands or bad installs. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier in the profiles.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter executes commands derived from Copilot output
IF the operator does not independently verify Copilot-generated steps before execution
mitigations: Require human review before any Open Interpreter command execution
Copy Copilot output into a checklist and verify each step
Disable Open Interpreter auto-run mode
Use Copilot only for suggestions, not operational instructions
requires-engineering: add a verification gate between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is tied to GitHub repo context and editor buffers, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine and uses model-provider APIs with user-configured keys. If regulated data or secrets are present locally, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data certification conflict.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are stored in the local filesystem or repo context
IF Open Interpreter sends that content to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Exclude regulated folders from the workspace
Use a local-only model for Open Interpreter
Rotate any exposed API keys
Review retention settings for both tools
requires-engineering: enforce data-class routing and residency controls
